## Active

### D-002 — A legacy memory file is refused until it is migrated

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · active_

add, close, move, index and format refuse a file that has no generated index block, because an
inserted entry would land next to prose the parser cannot describe. check stays permissive so it can
report what a legacy file still needs.

### D-003 — Package memory files must stay tracked by git

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · active_

The repository .gitignore ignores a bare todo.md, which also matched the package memory todo files:
migrated package todos were untracked and would never have been committed. The memory paths are
negated explicitly; keep that negation when the ignore rules change.

### D-066 — blong-dev sql falls back to the shared adapter's dev defaults

> _2026-08-21 · tools/blong-dev · active_

`blong-dev sql` failed with `Access denied for user ''@'...'` when `.blong_devrc` did not configure
a `srv.db` connection (the repo-root file only has `db.sql` for a remote ut-microservice database
and `_srv.db._google`), which forced `kubectl exec` into the MySQL pod: `readConnection` resolved to
`{}` and mysql2 connected as an anonymous user. `readConnection` now starts from the shared `srv.db`
adapter's dev defaults (`blong-admin`/`password` at `localhost:3306`) when resolving the default
`srv.db` key and layers `.blong_devrc` plus CLI overrides on top, with missing fields keeping the
defaults; custom `--config` keys stay empty when unconfigured, which preserves the
`--config mysql.sql` test. An `ensureDatabase` helper and a `derived` flag auto-create the derived
dev database (`${suite}-${user}`) when it is missing, mirroring the dev intent's
`createDatabase: true`. The `srv.db`-only fallback was chosen over applying defaults to every key
(which would break the custom-key contract), and auto-create applies only to the DERIVED database,
never to an explicit `--database`. Verified: 44/44 tap tests (13 sql tests including four new),
`tsc --noEmit` green, and a live run that auto-created `blong-access-kalin`.

### D-067 — blong-dev sql always allows multiple statements

> _2026-08-21 · tools/blong-dev · active_

Asked to run several `;`-separated statements in one query and return all their results, the command
now always enables mysql2's `multipleStatements: true`. With it, a single statement's result comes
back as-is (a rows array or a `ResultSetHeader`) while multiple statements are collected into an
ARRAY of result sets; `isMultiResult` detects the shape (an array whose every element is an array or
a `fieldCount`-bearing header) and `formatResultSet` renders it. JSON output emits a single result
set unchanged, keeping it backward compatible, or the array of result sets for multi; pretty output
labels each set `— result N`. Verified: 84/84 tap tests, `tsc --noEmit` green, and live runs showing
`[[rows],[rows]]` for two selects and `[header, header, [rows]]` for create/insert/select.

### D-001 — Memory files are written through blong-dev memory

> _2026-09-15 · tools/blong-dev · active_

The three root memory files (about 3050 lines) were slow to search and referenced each other by line
number. Every entry now has a stable id (one per kind, numbered in writing order), a
`date · area · status` meta line, a section that matches its status and a place in a generated index
at the top of the file, so an agent reads about 40 lines instead of a whole file. Package-specific
entries move to the package's `.github/memory/`; the root keeps cross-cutting, ci, docs and skills.

### D-195 — blong-dev log reads the record shape, payloads behind a flag

> _2026-09-17 · tools/blong-dev · active_

`blong-dev log` reads the store in the record shape the semantic logger writes, and hides payload
blobs unless `--payloads` is given, rather than trying to read both shapes. Records are located
through `service` and `context` (which the condensed line prints as the component), `operation`
(printed as the method) and `refs.trace` (printed as the trace id), so its `--name`, `--method` and
`--trace-id` filters work against what the logger actually writes. The existing cache was deleted
when this landed, because its entries were written in the pino shape and nothing reads them any
more.
